body:
## Problem

`_add_security_headers` was registered with `app.after_request`, so it ran for
EVERY response in the host application, not just this blueprint's routes. A
blueprint is a guest in someone else's app; setting response policy for routes it
doesn't own is wrong.

Concretely, an app mounting this blueprint alongside another blueprint would get
our `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'` (on HTML) and
`Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` on the OTHER blueprint's responses too. CSP breaks
the neighbor's inline scripts; `no-referrer` makes browsers send `Origin: null`
on same-site form POSTs, which an Origin-checking CSRF guard rejects (403).

(Reported via external review. Note the report's fix #2 — use `setdefault` — was
already in place, so we never *overwrote* a header the host set; but we still
*added* headers to responses we don't own, which is the same category of bug.)

## Why the obvious fix is wrong here

The report suggested swapping `app.after_request` for `@bp.after_request`
(Flask scopes it by `request.blueprint`). That does not work for THIS codebase:
the HTML routes that most need the headers — the invite landing page
(`/invite/<token>`, where `no-referrer` keeps the token out of the Referer
header) and the SPA (`/`) — are registered directly on the app, OUTSIDE any
url_prefix, per Spec §5's site-root URLs. `request.blueprint` is None for them,
so a blueprint-scoped hook would fire only for the `/api/v1/*` JSON routes and
silently DROP CSP / X-Frame-Options / no-referrer from exactly the pages that
need them.

## Fix (implemented)

Keep the single app-wide `after_request` hook (Flask can't scope after_request
to a subset of app-level routes), but have it self-limit to routes THIS
extension owns:
  - our API blueprint(s): `request.blueprint` in `app.extensions[EXTENSION_KEY]`
    (already keyed by our blueprint names for multi-mount config isolation), and
  - our site-root routes: `request.endpoint` in a per-app set of the endpoints we
    actually registered (invite_landing_view / android_apk / web_index +
    web_asset + web_favicon), recorded as each is registered.

Anything else — another blueprint's routes, an unrelated host route, a 404 for a
path we don't serve — is left untouched. Behavior is identical in the standalone
wheel deployment (we own the whole app there).

Files: server/src/shoppinglist_server/__init__.py (hook + ownership tracking),
tests/test_hardening.py (co-mounted-blueprint regression tests), server/README.md.
title: Blueprint set security headers app-wide instead of on its own routes
